title: Review encryption-key supersession and retirement against T_supp
description: Review the encryption lifecycle as a revocation and suppression boundary before rotation integration. Decide whether recipient-key supersession, old root and HistoryNode key_wrap retirement, content-frontier retirement, removed-device exclusion, content-reader eligibility, transition reservations and finalizations, causal retirement-batch claims, closed-pile transition closure, excluded purge operations, and purge-complete evidence belong in the global suppression or death-key match tree or remain explicit causal predecessor, authority, schedule, batch, operation, retirement, and local-erasure refs. Check backward, out-of-range, future, delayed, and archived wraps; different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch successor attempts; complete versus truncated reservation piles; operations included or excluded by explicit batch refs under reordered closed-pile delivery; removed or auth-only recipients; and the rule that suppression changes projection and closure but never rewrites stable validity. Resolve compositional cases where a valid wrap arrives only after completion, healing wraps a survivor later purged, or an independently valid purge operation excluded from one transition must rebase to the finalized recipient. Ensure no design treats hiding ciphertext as proof of key destruction, parks a transition fact waiting for missing closure, or uses a suppression timestamp or local arrival boundary to assign an operation to a generation. This bead is review and planning only. Any newly discovered revocation or suppression implementation problem becomes a separate bead and is not implemented here.
acceptance_criteria: Produce an arrival-order-independent matrix for recipient facts and P/S/T schedule claims, immutable batch commitments and exact operation refs, complete and truncated non-wrap reservation piles, included and excluded operation facts, full-reader proof, auth-only infra, local private and schedule state, generation-sealed or independently keyed cover, root and HistoryNode key_wrap facts including unseen and delayed wraps, content frontiers, removed devices, past ciphertext, and future ciphertext. For each transition identify stable validation, explicit refs and needs, closed-pile serialization and rejection, recovery eligibility, T_supp extraction and resolve_supp, projection hiding, local purge, write fence, recipient-generation trigger, operation-to-generation assignment, and publication boundary. Resolve whether new death or suppression keys and closure edges are required and add implementation beads rather than implementing them here; explicitly reconcile poc-16-x1o.16 through poc-16-x1o.21. Timestamps remain causally inert. The result must prevent auth-only recipients from obtaining material, block archived-wrap or sealed-cover resurrection after supersession without a local negative lookup, reject different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch forks, reject incomplete transition units without pending state or destructive effects, and ensure every excluded eligible operation causes another rotation rather than disappearing into a completed generation.

title: Benchmark cover growth, enclave handles, rotation, and rewrap fanout
description: Measure the operational cost of the chosen design under realistic and adversarial histories: dense/sparse authoring, random and clustered punctures, many workspaces, many devices, many live frontiers, offline recipients, recipient rotation, healing, and large files. Separate local KDF/cover work, hardware operations, durable ciphertext growth, T_fact/T_supp overhead, network wrap fanout, and restart/recovery time.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible benchmarks report p50, p95, p99, storage, and handle counts across documented sizes. Results demonstrate retained hardware state scales with active workspace-recipient generations rather than content count and compare cover growth with the theoretical tree bound. For the independently generated non-exportable hierarchy, record two handles per steady recipient generation and the three-handle P/S/T transition peak; any lower-peak provider must name and measure its alternative. Measure rotation separately for root loss; standard healing where every retired wrap-eligible or generation-sealed HistoryNode rotates despite no visible wrap; and, only if the ADR admits it, a non-wrappable, non-generation-bound, independently deletable cover mode that permits the first-F-only special case. Include write-fence drain latency under authoring and healing load, causal batch-claim closure, excluded-operation rebase recovery, P/S/T reservation and finalization overhead, competing-claim failure behavior, migration, and live-frontier, device, and cover rewrap fanout; report worst-case cadence. Keep regression guards that show a two-handle cap fails before predecessor destruction, capacity for the third handle completes and returns to two, and saved-state recovery succeeds. Document weaker snapshot and cloned-state guarantees.

title: Document migration, guarantees, operations, and release gates
description: Update DESIGN.md, docs/WORKSPACES.md, and operator and user documentation to replace stable dev_box content wrapping with rotating, reader-authorized recipient generations. Describe the KDF, canonical cover, puncture graph, causal recovery eligibility, delayed-wrap threat, content-frontier versus recipient rotation, full-reader versus auth-only infra boundary, generation writer fence, immutable causal retirement-batch claim and excluded-operation rebase, closed-pile non-parking transition delivery, recursive P/S/T schedule claim, non-wrap-eligible reservation and finalization boundary, steady and transition-peak handle counts, and suppression visibility versus purge completion. Plan versioned migration for existing plaintext content and keychain state, interrupted upgrades, mixed-version peers, provider capability changes, backups, cloned or rolled-back device state, device loss, and recovery. Include the accepted revocation and T_supp review plus poc-10 source lineage.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh-workspace walkthrough and an upgrade fixture both pass the complete test suite. Migration is restartable, never writes plaintext into synced facts, and either finishes on the new version or fails closed with recoverable old state. Documentation states exactly what purge complete guarantees on each provider tier, why a locally unseen wrap is possible, how delayed and offline peers affect eventual forward secrecy, why P-bound writers are fenced before survivor enumeration, why exact operation refs and pile closure—not arrival before a freeze—define a committed batch, why incomplete reservation piles reject without parking, why excluded operations rebase and may rotate again, why reservations cannot receive wraps, how P/S/T schedule and batch claims prevent immediate and deferred forks, why a non-exportable transition peaks at three handles, how a two-handle cap fails safely while three-handle capacity succeeds, how cloned state fails closed or weakens guarantees, how reader proofs exclude auth-only infra, why timestamps do not encode causality or winner selection, and which explicit refs and closure edges do. Release gates name adversarial and scale suites and require no unresolved P0 or P1 security findings.

title: Drive confidentiality purge from global suppression closure
description: Connect validated poc-16 suppression to encryption without putting suppression into stable fact validity. When resolve_supp/T_supp surfaces a valid deletion and its victims through pile closure, enqueue explicit coordinate-based puncture work after the suppression root/manifest publication boundary. Handle victim-before-deletion, deletion-before-victim, out-of-range discovery, future victims, duplicate sync, and restart. Projection disappearance and cryptographic purge are distinct states: UI may hide promptly, but only the local rotation/purge state machine can claim confidentiality completion.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests on multiple peers cover both arrival orders, out-of-range T_supp discovery, future matching facts, concurrent manifest readers, failure before/after suppression-root CAS, restart, duplicate delivery, and offline convergence. Stable validity is byte-identical before/after suppression; the closed pile contains the causal deletion evidence; no SQL/global lookup is used to decide validity; and purge is launched exactly once per explicit victim operation while safely resuming duplicates.

title: Integrate membership removal, frontier rotation, rewrap, and key healing
description: Keep membership removal content-frontier rotation separate from puncture-triggered recipient rotation. An authorized removal fact causally refs the membership, reader authority, and frontier it changes. A new monotonically linked frontier generates fresh F and wraps only to remaining eligible reader recipient successors. If recipient rotation invalidates predecessor wraps, normal key request and healing rewrap every still-live frontier to the successor: F only while live, otherwise canonical retained HistoryNode cover with exact coordinates and tombstone context—never a retired F or deleted leaf. Wherever healing permits a HistoryNode as a wrap source, that node is recovery-eligible before any particular wrap is observed; a later purge rotates even if its valid wrap was created remotely or arrives late. Specify offline peers, delayed wraps, simultaneous removal and purge, recipient successor forks, and recovery when a device has only part of the retained cover.
acceptance_criteria: Three-or-more-peer tests remove a device, rotate the content frontier, continue authoring, and prove the removed device and auth-only infra cannot open new content. Independent tests rotate a remaining recipient due to F purge and heal unrelated live root or cover material to its eligible successor. A new full-reader device joining a punctured frontier receives only canonical survivor cover, opens survivors, and cannot open deleted content. A valid cover wrap withheld until after its source node is purged cannot be opened by the rotated recipient. Out-of-order removal, reader-proof, frontier, recipient, and wrap facts converge through refs and closure, never timestamp ordering. Requests for retired F, retired recipients, removed or ineligible devices, or deleted coordinates fail.

title: Audit all secret copies and add adversarial forward-secrecy tests
description: Threat-model and test every place F, leaf, cover, recipient private material, decrypted plaintext, and archived wraps can survive: Python/Rust objects, caches, queues, SQLite tables/WAL/journals, temp files, blobs, crash dumps/logging, backup/export, treap piles, manifests, delivery logs, and enclave sealed state. Exercise post-purge compromise, stale snapshot, malicious re-delivery, peer lag, and interrupted rotation. File separate beads for revocation/suppression issues discovered; do not fold unrelated revocation fixes into this implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A storage-surface inventory links each secret to an owner and purge hook. Automated adversarial tests retain ciphertext plus old root and HistoryNode wraps, include a valid pre-purge wrap withheld on another peer, complete an initial F purge and at least one later eligible-cover purge, then deliver the withheld wrap and attempt every supported recovery path. All fail for the claimed tier while survivor content still opens. Memory and cache hooks verify eviction and best-effort zeroization. Backup, export, and log fixtures contain no plaintext or local private material. An auth-only infra fixture never receives reader-authorized key material. Any untestable platform guarantee is explicitly scoped and documented rather than asserted.

title: Rotate recipient eph generations on recovery-eligible key purge
description: Integrate purge-triggered recipient rotation as a resumable local state machine driven by the explicit retirement set and poc-16-x1o.16 through poc-16-x1o.21. A purge advances the recipient generation exactly once when it retires any secret recoverable through the current generation: F, a wrap-eligible HistoryNode, a generation-sealed equivalent, or material derivable through a retained generation root. Recovery eligibility is monotonic and causal from immutable secret kind plus source, sealing, recipient, and provider-policy refs; it never comes from visible-wrap inventory. Under the standard bounded provider, root and HistoryNode secrets are eligible and purge rotates even with no observed wrap; the first-F-only rule exists only for an explicit non-wrappable, non-generation-bound, non-root-derivable provider tier. From caller-supplied saved state, claim predecessor P and the immutable retirement-batch commitment, load the recursive schedule pair S/T and now-only fact timestamp, and publish a non-wrap-eligible reservation that explicitly refs every batch operation and carries its complete closed-pile dependency set. Resolve full P/S/T/batch equivalence before irreversible work; never add an operation merely because it arrived before a local boundary, and reject rather than park any incomplete reservation. Install the P generation write fence, drain or abort in-flight P-bound writers, validate the exact claimed operation closure, enumerate and migrate every survivor to S, and durably validate S/T. Only after every capacity-dependent claim, allocation, closure, migration, and T preparation succeeds may the transition retire old-generation wraps and destroy P private material. It then performs allocation-free promotion, publishes finalized S with commitment T, and completes exactly the committed operations. Every independently valid operation outside the batch—including one carried by a mismatched reservation—remains queued and rebases by explicit refs onto S; if recovery-eligible under S it enters a later unique batch and triggers the S-to-T rotation. Persist monotonic phases because database, manifest publication, fencing, schedule promotion, and hardware deletion are not one transaction. Retries reuse saved prepared state; timestamps never choose or order claims, operations, batches, or generations.
acceptance_criteria: Crash injection before and after predecessor plus batch claim, S/T load, complete reservation ingestion, full claim resolution, operation-closure validation, writer fence and drain, survivor migration, T validation, old-wrap purge, P destruction, allocation-free promotion, S finalization, excluded-operation rebase, and completion converges without exposing a reservation as a wrap target, losing survivors, changing batch membership by arrival, parking an incomplete claim, or claiming completion while old material works. Delayed P wraps cannot open after destruction. Standard healing rotates for every eligible cover purge; a first-F-only fixture is allowed only with the explicit weaker provider proof. The poc-16-x1o.16 barriers prove no P-bound authoring, seal, request, or healing commit lands after the fence or escapes the survivor scan. The poc-16-x1o.17, poc-16-x1o.18, poc-16-x1o.20, and poc-16-x1o.21 matrices prove different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are permanently invalid, only identical whole claims coalesce, closed-pile delivery order cannot change operation assignment, truncated claims reject with no pending state, three or more generations remain fork-free, a two-handle cap fails before P destruction, and a three-handle-capable non-exportable provider completes and returns to two. The poc-16-x1o.19 matrix proves every excluded valid operation rebases onto S and, when eligible, causes a second rotation; a remote peer wraps the target to S before that second purge and withholds the wrap, then destroyed S cannot open it. Neither concurrency nor retry uses timestamp arbitration, fid ranking, arrival ranking, or latest-row lookup. Locked hardware or capacity failure at every claim, fence, allocation, closure, migration, or T-preparation boundary fails closed without finalizing S, completing purge, or destroying P; crash or lock after destruction resumes allocation-free promotion from saved S/T. Auth-only infra cannot supply reader proof. Strong-tier rollback tests reject restored snapshots.

title: Implement bounded local secret provider and encrypted cover store
description: Implement the key-provider boundary selected by the hardware ADR: generate, use, and destroy active recipient ephemeral private handles; maintain the recursively unique schedule state that fixes transition pair P/(S,T); atomically authorize a caller-supplied immutable retirement-batch commitment as part of the one-time transition claim; envelope-seal F and retained-cover nodes to the active generation; enumerate and migrate live ciphertext records without exporting a hardware private key; expose generation-scoped writer leases, close-and-drain fencing, commit compare-and-set, and the selected schedule-and-batch claim capability; and report capabilities and recovery-eligibility metadata. For independently generated non-exportable keys, steady state holds active P plus staged S. Before P destruction, transition preparation verifies S and generates and durably protects S staged-next T, so the peak is three handles and no quota-dependent allocation remains after the irreversible boundary. Final promotion destroys P and changes durable generation state to the already existing S/T pair; the next transition advances the schedule to T/U under the same rule. Standard generation sealing makes every sealed cover node recovery-eligible, so the provider reports that causal property even if shared HistoryNode wraps are disabled. It does not choose operation membership, author recipient reservations or successors, or perform purge-triggered rotation; poc-16-x1o.16 through poc-16-x1o.20 and poc-16-x1o.10 consume the primitives and own those workflows. Keep stable identity and attestation operations separate from content unwrapping. An optional first-F-only provider mode may exist only if it stores cover under independently deletable, non-generation-bound keys and proves no active recipient key or retained root can unwrap archived node ciphertext. The software test provider models deletion, rollback, cloned state, and missing monotonic claims honestly rather than claiming Secure Enclave guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Contract tests run against an in-memory fault provider and every available real or software provider. They cover three or more P/S/T/U schedule advances; two-handle steady and three-handle transition-peak counts for the non-exportable hierarchy; full P/S/T/batch claim matching; rejection of a replay with the same P/S/T but a different batch; proof that P private material cannot derive S or T; pre-destruction preparation of T; allocation-free idempotent promotion to S/T; handle deletion; wrong generation and AAD; writer-lease acquisition and drain; post-fence commit rejection; partial migration primitives; locked hardware; restart; cloned and restored state; backup restore; transient-buffer zeroization where possible; and capability reporting. Quota exhaustion at a two-handle limit fails every non-exportable rotation before P destruction, while capacity for the documented third transition handle succeeds and returns to two after promotion. Any claimed lower-peak provider has a contract test for its alternative. Key creation, claim, fence, migration, or next-key preparation errors never report unusable state as durable, never destroy P, and destroy or track orphan allocations. After P destruction, promotion and finalization consume only validated durable S/T state; a lock or crash may delay completion but cannot require a new allocation or lose S. Provider retries use caller-supplied prepared state; causal operation selection, graph resolution, evidence rebasing, and end-to-end rotation remain downstream. Stress tests keep handles bounded by the documented per-recipient steady and transition constants, independent of content count. A generation-sealed HistoryNode is reported recovery-eligible; this bead does not rotate it. No stable root API can request or derive a retired generation.

title: Encrypt messages and files with KDF leaf keys
description: Replace plaintext message and file fact payloads with versioned AEAD ciphertext using the KDF leaf selected by the explicit content coordinate and frontier ref. Authenticate all clear routing/authorization/dependency fields as AAD. Define whether file descriptors and chunks use distinct derived subkeys/nonces, and preserve sealed-but-not-yet-openable projection so ciphertext may sync before the recipient has cover material. Keep plaintext out of durable fact bytes, treap piles, manifests, delivery logs, blob filenames/metadata, and ordinary projection rows.
acceptance_criteria: Realistic multi-peer tests author, sync, open, restart, and late-deliver messages plus small/large files; ciphertext-before-wrap later opens through dependency/key healing. Tampering with ciphertext, nonce, coordinate, frontier, channel, parent, signer, chunk index, or size fails closed. Raw scans of fact/blob/index/app databases, WAL/journal files, manifests, logs, and sync payloads find no test plaintext. Same prepared authoring input retries without consulting latest state.

title: Implement exact/range puncture and durable secret erasure
description: Port poc-10 exact leaf retirement and time-prefix or range chop. Given an explicit validated victim coordinate or range and content frontier, materialize survivor siblings, atomically replace the old cover with the canonical new cover, exact-delete the leaf, descend path, and F when applicable, purge canonical secret bytes and transient caches, and retain only non-secret tombstone and retirement evidence needed to prevent resurrection. Emit an explicit retirement set for every removed F, HistoryNode, and leaf secret. For each item, carry a recovery-eligibility class derived from immutable secret kind and explicit source, recipient-generation, sealing, and wrap-policy refs. A FrontierRoot or HistoryNode that protocol policy allows any peer to wrap is conservatively eligible even when no wrap is present in the local pile; local absence is never evidence of no delayed or archived wrap. Leaf-only material may be ineligible only when the protocol causally forbids it as a wrap or generation-seal source. Rotation consumes this explicit set; neither retry state nor recovery eligibility is inferred from timestamps, latest-row lookup, or observed wrap inventory.
acceptance_criteria: Property tests puncture random leaves and ranges in varying orders and compare decryptability with an oracle. The victim cannot be derived from any retained node while every live coordinate remains openable. Duplicate or reordered purge work is idempotent from explicit operation id and basis refs. Fault tests cover the local database transaction and canonical-byte and WAL cleanup. Root and HistoryNode retirement reports recovery eligibility when a valid wrap was created remotely and withheld, and when no shared wrap is allowed but the node is sealed to the current generation. Tests distinguish a causally non-wrappable and non-generation-bound transient secret, which may skip rotation, from the same secret with a wrap, generation-seal, or retained-root recovery ref, which rotates. No implementation proves ineligibility from an empty local wrap query.

title: Implement canonical retained-cover and lazy leaf derivation
description: Represent the decryptable remainder after punctures as the canonical prefix-free sibling cover from poc-10. Derive fresh leaves from F or the deepest retained covering sibling, materialize only what authoring/opening or a puncture needs, and reject a coordinate with no retained ancestor. Persist secret-bearing cover nodes only through the selected encrypted local-secret provider; public graph/pile state may carry coordinates and tombstones but never node secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Model/property tests compare randomized author/puncture/open sequences with a simple set-of-live-leaves oracle, prove the cover is prefix-free/non-overlapping and cannot cover a punctured coordinate, and show all surviving coordinates still derive the expected leaf. Restart tests reconstruct the same cover. Measurements demonstrate no one-key-per-content durable state: fresh operation stays near one root plus lazily used leaves, and p punctures grow with the tree cover bound rather than total content count.

title: Add content frontiers, reader-bound recipient successors, and key_wrap facts
description: Port poc-10 removal_frontier and local_key_secret, workspace-scoped local_recipient_key and recipient_key, and key_wrap design using poc-16 facts and closure. Initial and replacement content-frontier facts use explicit predecessor and authority refs and bind the scope chosen by poc-16-t9f.4; random F is local secret material and never shared plaintext. The local recipient private half and key-schedule state are protected through the selected provider. The shared recipient fact is self-signed by stable device identity, causally refs an eligible full-reader authority proof for the same scope, and carries the next-recipient public-key commitment fixed by the recursive schedule claim; sync-only or infra authority cannot satisfy that need. For transition P to S, the non-wrap reservation and finalization bind S, the next commitment T that S publishes, an immutable retirement-batch commitment, and explicit refs to every included purge operation. Each fetchable transition unit carries the full dependency-first closure; missing refs reject the unit and never park. A wrap-eligible S explicitly refs P, matches the full P/S/T/batch claim, publishes the matching T commitment, carries a still-eligible reader proof and finalized transition evidence, and retires P without latest-timestamp selection. Different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are structurally ineligible; multiple valid facts for the identical whole claim denote one transition rather than competing keys or batches. Provide the codec and need distinction for the non-wrap-eligible transition reservation completed by poc-16-x1o.17, poc-16-x1o.20, and poc-16-x1o.21: a reservation or staged public-key commitment is not a recipient and cannot satisfy request, proactive-share, healing, or key_wrap validation. Proactive sharing, key requests, and healing all need the same reader proof and a finalized recipient. A key_wrap binds scope, frontier, recipient generation and fact id, reader-authority ref, algorithm and version, WrappedSecretKind of FrontierRoot or HistoryNode, exact node coordinate, source and tombstone context, recovery-eligibility policy ref, authorized sender, and ciphertext as AEAD associated data. Root and HistoryNode sources permitted by healing are recovery-eligible whether or not a recipient has yet observed their wrap.
acceptance_criteria: Real X25519 plus AEAD tests cover initial F distribution, root and retained HistoryNode wraps, two full-reader peers, an auth-only infra peer, multiple frontiers per recipient, wrong scope, frontier, reader proof, secret kind, node coordinate, recipient or AAD, replay, tamper, predecessor from another device, successor before predecessor, duplicate delivery, retry, and concurrent successor attempts. Schema and closure tests across at least P/S/T/U reject a direct successor whose public key, published next commitment, or retirement-batch commitment differs from the provider claim; coalesce only identical P/S/T/batch retries; prove every included operation travels in the reservation pile by dependency-first closure; reject a truncated reservation without pending state; and prove a bare, losing, unresolved, incomplete, or abandoned reservation cannot be used as a recipient or key_wrap target. Only matching finalization evidence can enable S. The infra peer may sync and validate ciphertext but cannot publish an eligible content recipient, satisfy a request, or receive proactive or healing wraps. After finalized successor closure new wraps never target P, and delayed P wraps cannot be opened after private-key purge. A retired root or leaf cannot be mislabeled as a live HistoryNode. Shared facts contain only public or ciphertext material; local F, private keys, and schedule state never enter synced trees, piles, manifests, delivery logs, app projections, or sync. Schedule, batch, closed-delivery, and destructive-race tests belong to poc-16-x1o.18, poc-16-x1o.20, poc-16-x1o.21, and poc-16-x1o.17.

title: Specify explicit content coordinates and causal encryption refs
description: Define the shared and local fact shapes after poc-16-t9f.4 records workspace-frontier versus channel-frontier scope. A shared content fact carries an explicit fresh 256-bit content coordinate or equivalent collision-resistant prepared nonce, its scoped content-frontier ref, authorization refs, and ciphertext. Timestamp is captured as now on first authoring and may select the time-tree bucket only. Retry reuses saved prepared inputs and never queries the latest timestamp, key, or frontier to manufacture determinism. Derived local KDF and retirement artifacts carry no timestamp or copy the basis fact timestamp as inert metadata. Content-frontier and recipient-key successor facts explicitly name predecessors. Every recipient key also names a causal content-reader authority proof for the selected scope; auth-only membership is not such a proof. Key requests, proactive sharing, and key_wrap creation need that proof in closure. Each wrap names recipient, frontier, wrapped-secret kind, exact root or HistoryNode coordinate, and an explicit recovery-eligibility source or policy ref. Suppression and deletion name victim or death key so closure, not temporal comparison, relates facts.
acceptance_criteria: A schema and closure diagram plus codecs pin every ref, need, signed field, coordinate, recovery-eligibility bit or policy ref, reader-authority proof, and AEAD associated-data field. Tests prove two facts from one author with the same timestamp get distinct leaves; retrying a saved prepared command is byte-identical without a database read or clock call; out-of-order arrival converges by dependency closure; changing timestamp alone cannot grant authority, prove content-reader eligibility, select an active recipient, supersede a key, or satisfy a causal need; and a sync-only or infra participant cannot construct a recipient pile that satisfies wrap or healing eligibility.

title: Decide secure-hardware key hierarchy and purge guarantee tiers
description: Choose how poc-16 protects a potentially large retained KDF cover without one Secure Enclave or KeyStore handle per content key. Separate stable device signing and attestation identity from rotating content-unwrapping and key-schedule state. Compare independently generated non-exportable recipient ephemeral handles, a deterministic forward schedule guarded by rollback-resistant monotonic state, a permanent enclave root that can serve only the live schedule position, and any independently deletable non-generation-bound node-key option proposed for the first-F-only special case. Select a recursively anti-fork transition-claim primitive: for transition P to S, the predecessor state or rollback-resistant one-time claim fixes S, the next public key T that S will commit, and the immutable causal retirement-batch commitment; at the next transition the advanced state fixes T, U, and its next exact batch. Different-S, same-S/different-T, or same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are structurally invalid, while identical whole claims denote one transition. Account for the non-exportable hierarchy as two steady handles (active plus staged-next) and a three-handle transition peak (P, S, and S staged-next T before P destruction), unless an alternative proves a lower bound without post-destruction allocation, unbounded precomputation, or making P derive S or T. Reject a stable dev_box or root that can derive an old generation, reopen an archived wrap, unwrap an archived cover blob, reuse retired schedule state, or authorize two valid schedule or batch claims for one strong-tier predecessor. Define cover envelope encryption, survivor migration, writer fencing, schedule and batch claim, handle destruction and garbage collection, backup behavior, and guarantees possible on Apple, Android, TPM, and software-only providers.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR selects the primary hierarchy and portable fallback, with steady and transition-peak handle counts, backup and restore behavior, enclave API assumptions, crash windows, generation write-fence primitives, recursive unique-schedule plus causal-batch claim, and explicit normal-disk, hardware-backed, and rollback-resistant tiers. Tests perform three or more generations and prove each accepted transition claim P/(S,T,batch), then S/(T,U,batch2), is uniquely fixed; a successor public key, next commitment, or batch commitment that differs from the claim is invalid; and P private material alone cannot derive or open S or T. The independently generated non-exportable design budgets and exercises a three-handle peak before P destruction and returns to two; an alternative lower peak needs executable proof. A restored old sealed-state snapshot cannot recover retired keys or authorize a second claim in any tier claiming rollback resistance; software schedule designs state weaker snapshot and clone guarantees. The ADR includes rotate, migrate, destroy, claim, reservation, promotion, and finalization protocols and rejects deterministic old-key derivation from a retained root unless hardware monotonic state makes retired positions permanently inaccessible. If it permits a first-F-only mode, it proves retained cover nodes are neither shared-wrappable nor sealed or derivable through the active recipient generation or retained root; otherwise that mode is rejected.

title: Port the two-axis KDF core with cross-implementation vectors
description: Implement a small pure/executable core for F → power-of-two time-range splits → within-bucket 256-bit content-coordinate trie, preserving poc-10's domain separation (`topo time split v1`, `topo trie split v1`) unless the source-contract bead versions a change. Time is only an address into the first axis; the fresh content coordinate supplies uniqueness on the second. Make child derivation, coverage checks, coordinate encoding, and AEAD leaf-key derivation explicit and usable by running encryption/puncture code.
acceptance_criteria: Known-answer tests consume the frozen poc-10/poc-16 fixtures and cover root boundaries, left/right splits, minute/bucket edges, 256 trie bits, invalid geometry, domain separation, and distinct same-timestamp content coordinates. Property tests show a child is deterministic from explicit inputs and no API reads a clock or database. Runtime content encryption calls this verified/tested core rather than a parallel model.

title: Freeze poc-10 encryption lineage, threat model, and test vectors
description: Turn the relevant poc-10 lineage into the port source contract: 7f60936f and ad380cb4 for two-axis per-content puncturing; 536b13c3, 9b40f352, and bdaa60f6 for derive, wipe, and retained-sibling recovery; 178f198b through 341b8c37 to ed04d84f and 122cc471 for wrap-bound root-loss recipient rotation and purge; and later key healing that wraps retained HistoryNode secrets after F is gone. Resolve the historical wording in favor of key-purge-triggered rotation, then close the distributed composition gap: local absence of a wrap never proves a secret unrecoverable because another peer may delay a valid wrap, and forbidding shared wraps still does not prove safety when retained cover is envelope-sealed to the live recipient generation. Any root or retained node that can be a wrap source or is generation-bound is recovery-eligible from causal source, sealing, and policy refs; its purge advances the recipient generation even if this peer never observed a wrap. The original first-F-only result applies only when retained nodes are explicitly non-wrappable and non-generation-bound with no retained-root recovery path. Record as intentional poc-16 additions the generation write fence before survivor migration, immutable causally referenced retirement-batch claim with excluded-operation rebasing, closed-pile non-parking transition delivery, non-wrap reservation, recursive P/S/T then S/T/U schedule claim, and steady versus transition-peak handle budget. Record post-purge disk and snapshot attackers, availability tradeoffs, cloned-state boundary, content-reader eligibility, and the narrower contribution from poc-13 connection ephemeral-secret purge behavior. Identify every intentional deviation before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in design record maps each poc-10 source type and transition to its poc-16 counterpart, cites source commits, and contains state and secret ownership tables plus an adversary matrix. Versioned fixtures cover F generation, both KDF domains, splits and leaf derivation, root and HistoryNode wrap/open, first-F and later-cover purges, a remote wrap delivered after purge, generation-sealed cover, a predecessor-bound writer racing survivor scan, identical and mismatched P/S/T/batch reservations across S/T/U, a complete reservation carrying an included operation in closure with a later standalone duplicate, a truncated reservation rejected without parking, and an excluded operation observed before the accepted reservation. title: Puncturable content encryption + KDF history tree (poc-10 port)
description: Port poc-10 content encryption into poc-16: a random secret F per content frontier; a domain-separated two-axis KDF with time bucket as an address only and then a 256-bit content-coordinate trie; lazy leaf derivation; a canonical retained-sibling cover; exact/range puncture; encrypted content facts; and wrap-based recovery. Recipient rotation is driven by key purge, not by a wrap lookup. On each peer, a purge that retires any secret causally eligible for recovery through the current recipient generation—F or a HistoryNode that peers may wrap, or a generation-sealed local equivalent—triggers one eager recipient ephemeral-key rotation for that purge transition even when no wrap is visible locally. Recovery eligibility comes from immutable secret kind plus explicit source, sealing, and recipient policy refs and is monotonic; an unseen, delayed, archived, or locally sealed recovery path is always assumed possible. Under the standard bounded-provider design, both FrontierRoot and HistoryNode are wrap-eligible or envelope-sealed to the active generation, so each purge that retires one rotates. The poc-10 first-F-only result is an optional special case only if an explicit causal provider policy makes retained nodes both impossible shared-wrap sources and impossible to recover through the recipient generation or any retained root, for example through independently deletable non-generation-bound node keys with an honestly weaker snapshot tier. A transient leaf-only purge may skip only under the same no-recovery proof. For transition P to S, a non-wrap-eligible reservation carries a recursively unique P/S/T schedule claim and a provider-authorized immutable retirement-batch commitment. The reservation explicitly refs every included purge operation, and its serialized ingress unit carries the complete dependency-first closure; only identical P/S/T/batch retries coalesce. Different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are invalid. An incomplete reservation rejects immediately and never parks waiting for a missing operation. The transition fences and drains P-bound writers before scanning survivors, migrates all survivors, prepares the full S/T state, destroys P, and only then makes S wrap-eligible. Independently valid operation evidence outside the committed batch never joins retroactively, regardless of arrival: it rebases by explicit refs onto S and causes S-to-T rotation when recovery-eligible. If a provider cannot prove the unique schedule and batch claim, it retains P and fails closed. Keep content-frontier rotation for membership removal distinct from purge-triggered recipient rotation. A long-lived device identity may survive, but no stable dev_box, root operation, archived or delayed wrap, generation-sealed blob, post-fence write, sibling claim, partial pile, or rollbackable snapshot may reconstruct retired material in a tier claiming that protection. Retained covers are encrypted as data rather than one enclave handle per item. An independently generated non-exportable recipient hierarchy uses two handles at steady state and a three-handle P/S/T transition peak; a permanent hardware root or lower-handle design is allowed only with non-rollbackable schedule retirement and an explicit guarantee. Timestamps are authored as now and have zero causal, authorization, supersession, eligibility, operation-assignment, winner-selection, or retry-ordering weight; refs, needs, transition-batch claims, and pile closure establish relationships. Derived local artifacts carry no timestamp or copy a basis timestamp only as inert metadata. Compose confidentiality retirement with global suppression without putting suppression into stable validity.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed. Cross-implementation vectors pin the poc-10 KDF geometry and intentional poc-16 coordinate, fencing, recursive-schedule, causal-batch, closed-pile, evidence-rebase, and rotation deviations. Realistic multi-peer tests prove survivors remain decryptable while a suppressed or retired leaf, F, cover, old wrap, sealed blob, superseded private key, plaintext cache or WAL copy, and—on the strong tier—a restored sealed-state snapshot cannot recover deleted plaintext after completion. Delayed-wrap tests cover P and a later wrap to S followed by S-to-T purge. Barrier and multi-replica tests prove no P-bound writer commits after the fence, every pre-fence survivor migrates, reservations cannot receive wraps, different-S, same-S/different-T, and same-P/S/T/different-batch siblings are invalid across at least P/S/T/U, and excluded operation evidence rebases and completes in a later rotation. Identical accepted graphs yield identical operation-to-generation assignments under every closed-pile delivery order: a causally included operation rides the reservation closure and any later standalone copy deduplicates, while an excluded operation observed early remains queued for S. Truncated reservation piles reject without pending state or destructive side effects, then the same prepared fact succeeds when resent with its complete closure. The non-exportable provider proves two steady handles, succeeds through a three-handle transition peak, returns to two, and fails closed before P destruction when capped at two. Fault injection proves retries resume from saved state, never create timestamp or causal data from lookup, rotate once for each committed transition batch with recovery-eligible work, and skip only under explicit no-recovery policy. Auth-only infra lacks reader proof for recipients, requests, proactive shares, or healing wraps. Scale results show secret state grows with canonical cover and handles with active recipient generations rather than content count, and measure fence, rebase, fanout, healing, conservative rotation, and rewrap costs. Documentation distinguishes storage deletion, hardware deletion, rollback-resistant erasure, and weaker clone or snapshot tiers.

The current chained-auth fix prevents an evicted issuer from laundering a mint through a newly delegated user/device closure, but it does not stop an already-active colluder from transporting the evicted key's future messages, admin grants, or evictions. Preserve the current branch's stable-validation/history-independence constraints; investigate and choose the enforcement seam rather than patching it opportunistically.
acceptance_criteria: Add a realistic regression that demonstrates relay by a distinct active member; specify direct authorship and delegated user/device/admin behavior after removal; reject post-removal authority at a protocol seam that remains arrival-order-independent and convergent; cover the chosen behavior in black-box multi-peer tests and document the token/drain threat model.

title: PROOF: surface out-of-range victims by treap traversal only, zero SQL

(1) closure_sync(Q) on T_fact yields D but MISSES out-of-range victims (surface the bug). (2) supp_walk(T_supp, prefix=chan=X) surfaces them. Assert: (a) surfaced==true chan=X set (ground truth from seed); (b) treap node fetches only — instrumented counting store, ZERO idx/SQL calls, fetch count O(matches+depth) not O(M); (c) project(closure) suppresses every chan=X fact in- and out-of-range; (d) shuffled build ⇒ byte-identical T_supp root. Mirrors bench/bench_sync.py + hoist prototype.
notes: Landed deterministic zero-SQL proof in tests/test_suppression_proof.py: Q contains deletion + one in-range target while 20 same-group targets are outside Q; T_supp returns the exact 22-member group separately from dependency-closed topological transport context; all targets mask, deletion survives; history-independent root and concurrent-root convergence covered. Instrumented reads are bounded by matches+depth and <10% of stored objects. Full suite: 264 passed, 1 skipped. Independent agent review APPROVED with no blockers and independently confirmed near-flat unique reads through 32,001 participants. Fable review skipped per user authorization (unavailable).
close_reason: Closed

Validation: 262 passed/1 skipped; compileall/diff check green. Independent agent audited 469 pathological groups, lexical extremes, six multi-group permutations, pruning/no-SQL, and APPROVED. Fable waived by user.

title: Incremental fold on upload + two-root merge O(diff)
description: Event-driven incremental fold: a new pile folds in O(pile + log N) via path-copy, O(log N) memory. Restore a genuinely bounded two-root merge for semantic T_fact roots: merge(A,B)=root(A union B) with union-wide canonical offer/need resolution, without the correctness fallback's full scan/rebuild. Add authenticated provider/dependent summary metadata or an equivalently proven index; never preserve a side-local dependency graph when the union selects another provider.
notes:
Reopened after 808.9 independent review found the prior O(diff) close was valid only for fixed dependency maps. Legitimate concurrent provider/consumer roots can rewire canonical deps outside changed key ranges. The current safe tree.merge detects offers/declared needs, scans both roots, rebuilds proof ranks, and stages a deterministic full root. This bead is complete only when semantic roots regain a bounded merge without sacrificing the canonical-provider regressions. jbg.3 amortization and jbg.9 SEC remain downstream.
The bounded path is now explicit as tree.merge(..., prevalidated=True): only a caller that already authenticated both published roots may select it; all incorporated deltas remain checked. Any provider-summary solution must also prove enough root semantics to cross this trust boundary without an O(n) rescan.
Correct regression name is test_merge_enforces_union_wide_canonical_provider_graph. Root summaries/provider metadata must also commit enough information to prove byte-identical settle placement before prevalidated=True; fact-set validity alone is insufficient.

title: Non-serialized root: append-only roots set + amortized merge (drop the lease)
description: Publish roots into an append-only roots/ set; truth = merge(live roots), never clobbered. Amortize merge/sweep into every fold + authoritative read (deterministic merges dedup by hash, no storm). CAS-pointer (S3 If-Match / R2 onlyIf) and blind-LWW+sweep as variants. Remove the single-writer lease as the default; lease/DO becomes a per-workspace opt-in.
notes:
808.9 correctness review exposed a required merge distinction. tree.merge is O(diff) only when added facts have no offers and no declared needs. Otherwise either side's canonical provider graph can rewire outside the differing ranges, so the landed safe path loads the union, rebuilds proof ranks, validates canonical topo order, and stages a full deterministic root. This bead must amortize that correctness fallback for append-only roots (for example with authenticated provider summaries/index metadata); it must not restore the history-dependent path fold. Regression: test_merge_rebuilds_union_wide_canonical_provider_graph.
808.9 now makes root trust explicit: tree.merge validates by default; an append-only-root worker may use prevalidated=True only after authenticating both published roots (durable-only facts, canonical closure, derived metadata). Preserve that boundary while amortizing canonical fallback.

title: Make index generation stamping exception-safe

acceptance_criteria: A fault between root and version stamp writes leaves no open transaction; the retained pile retries in the same process and index/app stamps converge to the published root.
